tasks.title: Replace the battery of a TV remote
tasks.description: With a dexterous hand (Sharpa Wave by default, or Wuji Hand 2.2) on a Tianji Marvin arm, press the latch tab and slide open a remote's battery door, move the old gray AA cell from its slot into a receiving tray, seat a new green AA cell with correct polarity and slide the door shut until it latches; drops, knock-offs and a displaced remote fail the episode at once.
tasks.mechanism: passive sliding battery door with a spring-loaded latch tab and fixed latch stop, free AA cells, free remote and tray
tasks.instruction: Replace the battery of a TV remote that lies on the table. The remote's sliding battery door is shut and latched over a one-cell compartment holding an old gray AA cell; a new green AA cell lies on the table and an empty receiving tray stands beside the remote. In this order: (1) release the door latch by pressing the door's spring-loaded thumb tab down and slide the door open until it is at least 0.060 m open (full travel 0.085 m); (2) move the gray cell out of the compartment into the tray, where it must rest on the tray floor: its centre inside the tray's inner box (|x| <= 0.037 m, |y| <= 0.032 m in the tray frame) and at most 0.014 m above the tray origin (the floor top is 0.003 m above the origin; a resting cell's centre is about 0.010 m above it), touching the tray floor, with no hand contact; (3) seat the green cell in the compartment slot with correct polarity: its centre within 5 mm (along the slot), 3 mm (across) and 2 mm (height) of the slot centre, lying on both cradle ribs, and its + end toward the gold contact (cell axis within 10 degrees of the remote's long axis, + end at the gold contact); (4) slide the door shut and let the latch engage: at most 0.002 m open with the thumb tab released (pressed at most 0.0015 m), so its hook sits in front of the latch stop. Then release everything: with no hand contact on the remote, door, tray or either cell, the gray cell still in the tray, the green cell still seated, the door still shut and latched and every task object at rest (linear speed of its body origin <= 0.02 m/s, angular speed <= 0.5 rad/s; for the cells and the tray the origin is the centre of mass), the condition must hold for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; each stage counts only after the previous ones, and partial completion never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when any cell, the door, the remote or the tray falls below the table top (z < 0.30 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [-0.37, 0.47] m, y in [-0.34, 0.34] m, z in [0.30, 0.80] m, when any of them touches the floor, when the remote slides more than 0.03 m or tilts more than 15 degrees, when the tray slides more than 0.03 m or tilts more than 15 degrees, when the gray cell touches the table top, when the green cell touches the table top again after it has been lifted (lifted: at a control it is clear of the table and its centre is more than 0.01 m above its start height), when a cell without hand contact moves down faster than 0.886 m/s (the speed of a free drop from 0.04 m), or a cell touching nothing at all (no hand, no surface) moves down faster than 0.5 m/s (there is no grace period; a later catch does not undo it), when the parked left arm or the left hand touches the remote, its door, the tray or a cell (left_arm_contact; moving the left arm is not blocked, but the task is done by the right arm and hand), or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets (arm joints and fingers) are allowed; no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. The episode allows at most 6000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.
tasks.modeling: Tianji Marvin stand with two 7-DoF arms (right arm and hand work, left arm parked) at the table; free rigid remote at the source size (160 x 64 mm shell, 94 x 52 mm cavity; 0.35 kg incl. ballast, rubber feet), passive sliding battery door (slide joint, 0.085 m travel, end stops, source damping 0.1 and 0.08 N friction) with the source latch: a spring-loaded thumb tab (slide joint, 0..5 mm, 120 N/m) carrying a hook that sits in front of a fixed latch stop when the door is shut (opening and closing need the tab pressed about 2.9-4.5 mm), one-cell compartment with two cradle ribs between fixed end terminals (3 mm play; the source's compressible negative spring is not modelled), free rigid AA cells (23 g cylinders), free receiving tray. No electrical simulation.
